statement: Fix q in (0, r*). For p > q let V_p = t(p,q) U_p - U_q, with t = q W_q / (p W_p). The unit-edge cube y* is an equilibrium of V_p for every p. Let S = y* + T^perp be the O_h-invariant slice, where T is the space of rigid infinitesimal motions at y*, and let mu = p - P_A(q). There exist eps > 0 and a neighbourhood N of y* in S such that, for |mu| < eps, the equilibria of V_p in N are exactly: (1) the cube y*; (2) for mu > 0 only, x_pm(p) = y* pm a(p) e_A + beta(p) e_br, with a(p) > 0, beta(p) = O(a(p)^2), and a(p)^2 = 6 q W_q |h_A'(P_A(q))| mu / c4(q) + O(mu^2), where c4(q) > 0. x_+ and x_- are exchanged by D(-I), and each has point group T_d. For 0 < mu < eps the reduced potential has a strict local maximum at a = 0 and strict local minima at a = pm a(p): the pitchfork is supercritical in the energy sense.

H0.claim: V_p is real-analytic near (y*, P_A(q)), invariant under O_h and E(3); y* is an equilibrium

H0.distances.claim: the pair distances of y* are 1, sqrt2, sqrt3 (all >= 1), so V_p is analytic near y*

H0.Oh.claim: V is O_h-invariant for any pair potential; D(R) is orthogonal

H0.E3.claim: a pair energy depends only on pair distances, so it is E(3)-invariant

H0.equilibrium.claim: grad V(y*) lies in Fix(O_h) = span{e_br} (A1g has multiplicity 1); V_b = 0 exactly when A = t(p, q)

H1.claim: Z2 evenness: V_red(-a, mu) = V_red(a, mu), so d_a V_red = a G(a^2, mu) with G analytic

H1.character.claim: D(R) e_A = chi_A2u(R) e_A for all 48 R

H1.inversion.claim: D(-I) e_A = -e_A and D(-I) y* = y*

H1.complements.claim: D(R) orthogonal => orthogonal complements of O_h-invariant subspaces are invariant; the rigid-motion space T at the O_h-fixed y* is O_h-invariant
H1.complements.ref: linear algebra; D(R) maps E(3)-orbits to E(3)-orbits

H1.LS.claim: the equivariant Lyapunov-Schmidt reduction inherits the symmetry
H1.LS.ref: Golubitsky, Stewart & Schaeffer, Singularities and Groups in Bifurcation Theory, Vol. II (Springer, 1988)

H1.analytic.claim: V_p is real-analytic in (x, p), so V_red is analytic (analytic implicit function theorem); an odd analytic g(a, mu) equals a G(a^2, mu) with G analytic
H1.analytic.ref: analytic implicit function theorem; power series

H2.claim: at p = P_A(q): ker Hess V_p(y*) = T + span{e_A}

H2.multiplicity.claim: A2u has multiplicity 1 in Gamma_24; its isotypic component is span{e_A}

H2.eigenvector.claim: H e_A = V_aa e_A for any pair potential

H2.V_aa.claim: V_aa = q W_q [h_A(p) - h_A(q)] at the equilibrium; h_A is Paper 2's

H2.rigid.claim: translations and rotations lie in the kernel at the equilibrium

H2.Theorem 4'.claim: on p = P_A(q), 0 < q < r*, the only zero modes besides the rigid motions are A2u; the two curves never meet

H3.identity.claim: lambda(mu) = V_aa = q W_q [h_A(P_A(q) + mu) - h_A(q)] exactly for every p, because e_A is an exact eigenvector; so lambda(0) = 0 and lambda'(0) = q W_q h_A'(P_A(q))

Lemma A.claim: h_A has a unique maximum at r*, increases on (0, r*) from h_A(0+) = -6/7, decreases strictly on (r*, inf); P_A(q) > r* is the unique p > r* with h_A(p) = h_A(q)

H4.claim: c4(q) > 0 for every q in (0, r*) (Corollary M)

H4.LS formula.claim: c4 = V_aaaa - 3 <b, H_perp^-1 b>, b = D^3 V[e_A, e_A, .] (quartic coefficient of the Lyapunov-Schmidt reduced function)
H4.LS formula.ref: Golubitsky & Schaeffer, Singularities and Groups in Bifurcation Theory, Vol. I (Springer, 1985)

H4.b.claim: b = V_aab e_br and H e_br = V_bb e_br, so <b, H_perp^-1 b> = V_aab^2 / V_bb

H4.closed forms.claim: V_bb, V_aab, V_aaaa = q W_q [g(p) - g(q)] with the closed forms g_B, g_3, g_4

H4.scale-free.claim: on the curve c4 = (16/3) q W_q [m(p) - m(q)] (foliation lemma, scale-free chain, series coefficients of the T_d family); m is the V0.1-dev closed form

Lemma M.claim: m'(r) >= L_min = 161457/262144 > 0 on [0, 16/5] (Arb certificate, independent checker)

reduction.claim: equilibria in the slice near y* <-> zeros of d_a V_red; the solution w lies in Fix(T_d) ∩ e_A^perp = span{e_br}

reduction.slice.claim: for E(3)-invariant V, critical points of V restricted to the slice y* + T^perp near y* are equilibria, and conversely
reduction.slice.ref: slice argument; e.g. Golubitsky, Stewart & Schaeffer, Singularities and Groups in Bifurcation Theory, Vol. II (Springer, 1988)

reduction.LS.claim: Lyapunov-Schmidt reduction with parameter (implicit function theorem); the solution w(a, mu) is unique and O_h-equivariant
reduction.LS.ref: Golubitsky & Schaeffer, Singularities and Groups in Bifurcation Theory, Vol. I (Springer, 1985); Golubitsky, Stewart & Schaeffer, Singularities and Groups in Bifurcation Theory, Vol. II (Springer, 1988)

reduction.Fix.claim: the stabiliser of e_A is T_d, and Fix(T_d) = span{e_br, e_A}

branch side.claim: G(0,0) = 0, G_mu = lambda'(0) < 0, G_s = c4/6 > 0 => the nontrivial zeros form one curve mu = mu*(s), mu*'(0) = -c4/(6 lambda'(0)) > 0, so a^2 > 0 forces mu > 0; on it d^2 V_red/da^2 = 2 a^2 G_s = -2 lambda(mu) + O(mu^2) > 0, and at a = 0 it is lambda(mu) < 0

IFT.claim: implicit function theorem; Z2 pitchfork recognition
IFT.ref: Golubitsky & Schaeffer, Singularities and Groups in Bifurcation Theory, Vol. I (Springer, 1985)
